A police report was put up by the State through officer-in-charge of the police station Badarpur before the concerned Metropolitan Magistrate with the view to take cognizance of offence under section 326A of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (in short 'IPC') against the accused Yamin @ Aamin for having committed the said offence and to proceed with the case.

2. As per the police report, on 21.09.2015, this case FIR was registered against the accused Yamin @
Aamin for the offence under section 326A of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
3.

As per the police report, on 20.09.2015, DD No. 45A was assigned to Head Constable Rajender and Assistant Sub-Inspector Mahender, who was on patrolling in the area and was informed on wireless set and they reached the place of incident and met the injured Smt. Saroj who informed that Aamin had thrown acid on her back which was badly itching; in the meanwhile, the PCR Van reached at the spot and the injured was got sent to the hospital for treatment, thereafter, ASI Mahender along with accompanying staff made search for eye-witness but found none.

5.

As per the police report, it is, inter-alia, stated by the complainant in her complaint that on 20.09.2015, she had visited her brother Ashok @ Tinku from Dabri for taking money for the expenses and after alighting the bus at Onida Bus-Stand, Gautam Puri and proceeded for her brother's house on foot with her brother and when she reached near Kali Mandir, on seeing Salman,

6. It is further stated by the complainant that when she went to the Toilet near the police booth to ease out herself, Yamin @ Aamin came in the bathroom from backside and threw Acid like liquid on her back due to which she felt acute heat and she ran after Aamin but he managed to flee; that she again called at 100 number and went to the house of Yamin @ Aamin and bolted the door of his house from outside and ran towards the police post and the PCR van came there; that she was feeling lots of burn and her clothes were also brunt and one lady gave clothes i.e. suit salwar to her and she changed her clothes; that she kept her burnt suit in a polythene and she was taken to the Safdarjung hospital by the PCR van and she was admitted there for treatment.

7. It is further stated by the complainant that Salman had forcibly committed sexual onslaught on her and she had got a case FIR No. 1198/15 under section 376 IPC against him and he was absconding in that case and that was why she had caught Salman on seeing him in Gautam Puri.
It is further stated by the complainant that appropriate action as per law should be taken against the offender.

8. It is further reported in the police report that the doctor handed over a sealed pullanda containing the clothes of the injured worn by her at the time of incident to ASI Mahender which was seized by ASI Mahender and, thereafter, ASI Mahender along with SI Ranbir Singh came to the police station and discussed the entire facts and circumstances with officer-in- charge of the police station.

9. It is further reported in the police report that from contents of the complaint, result of MLC and injury on the person of the complainant, the offence under section 326A IPC has been made out,
therefore, a case under that section was got registered and further investigation was taken up by Sub- Inspector Ranbir Singh.

10. sentences.text: (a) The presence of an injured eye-witness at the time and place of the occurrence cannot be doubted unless there are material contradictions in his deposition.
(b) Unless, it is otherwise established by the evidence, it must be believed that an injured witness would not allow the real culprits to escape and falsely implicate the accused.
(c) The evidence of an injured witness is always of great value to the prosecution and it cannot be doubted on account of some embellishment in natural conduct or minor contradictions.

(d) If there be any exaggeration or immaterial embellishments in the evidence of an injured witness, then such contradiction, exaggeration or embellishment should be discarded from the evidence of injured, but not the whole evidence.

The essential ingredients of offence under section 326A IPC are as follows:
